title: Signature World-Loom
description: Higgins' world-loom weaves alternate worlds as threads on a visible loom: each changed assumption is a colored thread, and the woven cloth shows exactly which assumptions each world depends on. No hidden threads — every world displays its weave.

demo.code:
import random
random.seed(1001)
x_obs=1.0; x_cf=0.0; n=500
# structural model: U ~ N(0,1); Y = 2*X + U. Observe X=x_obs; counterfactual: X had been x_cf.
U=[random.gauss(0,1) for _ in range(n)]
Y_obs=[2*x_obs+u for u in U]
Y_cf=[2*x_cf+u for u in U]
eff=sum(y_cf-y_o for y_cf,y_o in zip(Y_cf,Y_obs))/n
print(f"observed_mean={sum(Y_obs)/n:.3f} counterfactual_mean={sum(Y_cf)/n:.3f}")
print(f"individual_effect={eff:.3f} (truth={(2*(x_cf-x_obs)):.3f})")
print("DEMO_OK")
demo.note: Runnable demo program verified by execution during the database build.

architecture: Assumptions register as threads with colors; worlds are woven by selecting threads. The cloth renderer shows thread intersections, so shared assumptions between worlds are visible at a glance.
